verses.text: Abimelek son of Jerub-Baal went to his mother's brothers in Shechem. He said to them and to all his mother's family,
"Ask all the leaders of Shechem, 'Which is better for you: to have all seventy sons of Jerub-Baal rule over you, or just one man?' Remember, I am your own flesh and blood."
His mother's brothers told all this to the leaders of Shechem, and they decided to follow Abimelek, because they said, "He is our relative."
They gave him seventy pieces of silver from the temple of Baal-Berith. With it Abimelek hired worthless, reckless men, and they followed him.
He went to his father's home in Ophrah, and on one stone he murdered his seventy brothers, the sons of Jerub-Baal. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerub-Baal, escaped by hiding.
Then all the leaders of Shechem and Beth Millo gathered beside the big tree at the stone pillar in Shechem and made Abimelek king.
When Jotham was told about this, he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted to them, "Listen to me, leaders of Shechem, so that God may listen to you!
One day the trees went out to choose a king for themselves. They said to the olive tree, 'Be our king.'
But the olive tree answered, 'Should I give up my oil, which is used to honour gods and people, just to sway over the trees?'
Next the trees said to the fig tree, 'Come and be our king.'
But the fig tree replied, 'Should I give up my sweet, good fruit, just to sway over the trees?'
Then the trees said to the vine, 'Come and be our king.'
But the vine answered, 'Should I give up my new wine, which cheers gods and people, just to sway over the trees?'
Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, 'Come and be our king.'
The thornbush said to the trees, 'If you really want to make me your king, come and rest in my shade. But if not, let fire come out of the thornbush and burn up the cedars of Lebanon!'
Now, have you acted honestly and in good faith by making Abimelek king? Have you been fair to Jerub-Baal and his family? Have you treated him as he deserved?
Remember, my father fought for you. He risked his life to save you from Midian.

But today you have turned against my father's family. You have murdered his seventy sons on one stone, and made Abimelek, the son of his slave woman, king over the leaders of Shechem, just because he is your relative.
So if you have acted honestly and in good faith toward Jerub-Baal and his family today, then may you be happy with Abimelek, and may he be happy with you!
But if not, let fire come out from Abimelek and burn up you leaders of Shechem and Beth Millo. And let fire come out from you leaders of Shechem and Beth Millo and burn up Abimelek!"
Then Jotham ran away. He escaped to Beer and lived there, because he was afraid of his brother Abimelek.
Abimelek ruled over Israel for three years.
Then God sent an evil spirit to cause trouble between Abimelek and the leaders of Shechem, and they turned against Abimelek.

God did this so that the crime against Jerub-Baal's seventy sons, the spilling of their blood, would be paid back on their brother Abimelek, who murdered them, and on the leaders of Shechem, who helped him do it.
To work against him, the leaders of Shechem put men on the hilltops to wait in hiding, and they robbed everyone who passed by. This was reported to Abimelek.
Then Gaal son of Ebed moved into Shechem with his brothers, and the leaders of Shechem trusted him.
They went out into the fields, picked the grapes, crushed them, and held a festival. They went into the temple of their god, ate and drank, and cursed Abimelek.

Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelek, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not Jerub-Baal's son, and is not Zebul his officer? Serve the family of Hamor, Shechem's father! Why should we serve Abimelek?
If only these people were under my command! Then I would get rid of him." And he challenged Abimelek, "Gather your whole army and come out!"
When Zebul, the governor of the city, heard what Gaal son of Ebed said, he was very angry.
He secretly sent messengers to Abimelek, saying, "Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you.
So tonight, you and your men should come and hide in the fields.
In the morning, at sunrise, attack the city. When Gaal and his men come out against you, do whatever you can to them."
So Abimelek and all his troops set out by night and hid near Shechem in four groups.
Gaal son of Ebed had gone out and was standing at the entrance of the city gate just as Abimelek and his troops came out of their hiding place.
When Gaal saw them, he said to Zebul, "Look, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains!" Zebul replied, "You are seeing the shadows of the mountains and thinking they are men."
But Gaal spoke up again: "Look, people are coming down from the centre of the land, and one group is coming from the direction of the fortune-tellers' tree."
Then Zebul said to him, "Where is your big talk now, you who said, 'Who is Abimelek that we should serve him?' Are these not the men you made fun of? Go out and fight them!"
So Gaal led the leaders of Shechem out and fought Abimelek.
Abimelek chased him, and Gaal ran away. Many were wounded and fell all the way to the entrance of the gate.
Then Abimelek stayed in Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem so they could no longer live there.
The next day the people of Shechem went out to the fields, and this was reported to Abimelek.
So he took his men, divided them into three groups and hid in the fields. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose up and attacked them.
Abimelek and the groups with him rushed forward and took their position at the entrance of the city gate. Then two groups attacked those in the fields and struck them down.
Abimelek attacked the city all that day until he captured it and killed its people. Then he destroyed the city and scattered salt over it.
When the leaders in the tower of Shechem heard this, they went into the stronghold of the temple of El-Berith.
Abimelek heard that they had gathered there.
So he and all his men went up Mount Zalmon. He took an axe, cut off some branches and put them on his shoulders. He told the men with him, "Quick! Do what you have seen me do!"

So all the men cut branches and followed Abimelek. They piled them against the stronghold and set it on fire with the people inside. So all the people in the tower of Shechem, about a thousand men and women, also died.
Next Abimelek went to Thebez. He surrounded it and captured it.
But inside the city there was a strong tower, and all the men and women of the city ran into it. They locked themselves in and climbed up onto the roof of the tower.
Abimelek went to the tower and attacked it. As he came near the entrance of the tower to set it on fire,
a woman dropped a large grinding stone on his head and cracked his skull.
He quickly called to the young man who carried his weapons, "Draw your sword and kill me, so that people will not say, 'A woman killed him.'" So the young man stabbed him, and he died.
When the Israelites saw that Abimelek was dead, they all went home.
In this way God paid Abimelek back for the evil he had done to his father by murdering his seventy brothers.
God also made the men of Shechem pay for all their evil. The curse of Jotham son of Jerub-Baal came upon them.
